description.narrative:
Through a delegated cooperation agreement with United Kingdom's Foreign and Commonwealth Development Office (UK FCDO) the outcome of this project is to sustain Syrian Civil Defense (SCD) operations to provide essential services in northwest Syria so that needs of affected populations are better met to save lives, ensure their safety, and support accountability to contribute to the stabilisation of Northwest (NW) Syria. This outcome supports short- and medium-term stabilisation needs in Syria by contributing to preventing displacement and by making a moderate actor an alternative to extremism through the provision of essential and life-saving services and by strengthening community resilience.
The SCD is one of the few impartial service providers in northwest Syria, with a trained volunteer force delivering essential and life-saving services. In periods of low violence, it provides civilian services such as repairing water and electricity infrastructure, and its importance has grown as moderate opposition service providers have withdrawn. During escalations in violence, it delivers emergency response including search and rescue, emergency medical care, and early warning systems to reduce civilian casualties. It also monitors ceasefires and informs the international community about the humanitarian situation, thereby contributing significantly to regional stability despite broader destabilising forces.
